prompt:
Bug report: cooking bechamel today took the new milk (lot HD-1026) although lot HD-1022 expires tomorrow. Fix it and add a regression test.

Work on your own; nobody will answer questions. When you finish, report: status `done` if you did the task, `not_found` if something the task names does not exist, `blocked` if you could not do it; `answer` holds any answer the task asks for (otherwise one short sentence); `changed` lists the files you changed.

report.answer: Fixed. Stock was being taken from the most recently received batch first, which is why cooking took HD-1026. In `src/domain/batches.js`, `consumptionOrder` now follows the first-expired, first-out rule in `docs/DATA.md`: the batch that expires first goes first, batches with no expiry date go last, and ties go to the batch received first, then the lower id. I added two regression tests to `tests/stock.test.js`. One checks that cooking bechamel takes lot HD-1022 and leaves HD-1026 untouched; the other checks the full ordering. Both tests fail without the fix and pass with it. All 28 tests and the lint check pass, and the fix has a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md`.

check.why: FEFO by the data rules, with a regression test
